His list is led by the movement disorders in his title: Parkinson's disease and atypical parkinsonism, dystonia and tremor disorders, deep brain stimulation, botulinum toxin therapy and neuro rehabilitation for movement disorders. Alongside these he manages epilepsy and drug-resistant epilepsy with EEG, acute ischemic stroke with IV thrombolysis, post-stroke neurological care and neuropathic pain.

He read MBBS at the University College of Medical Sciences in New Delhi with distinctions in multiple subjects, including physiology and pharmacology, took his MD in internal medicine at Lady Hardinge Medical College, and his DM in neurology at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences. His post-DM fellowship in movement disorders was at Artemis Hospital in Gurugram, where he now practises.

A dedicated fellowship after the DM is what narrows a general neurology training to the movement disorders his post is named for, and it explains a list on which deep brain stimulation and botulinum toxin appear rather than being referred elsewhere.

He received a Presidential Gold Medal and a Department of Biotechnology scholarship in 2008 for scoring 100 percent in biology in his twelfth standard, won the north zone Torrent Young Scholars Award in neurology in 2021, and presented an abstract and poster at the American Thyroid Association Conference in 2017.

He is a member of the Indian Academy of Neurology, the Movement Disorder Society International and its Indian body, the Delhi Neurological Association, the Indian Association of Physicians and the Indian Medical Association.

dr-subhash-kaul.bio:
Dr. Subhash Kaul is a Senior Consultant Neurologist at KIMS Hospitals, Secunderabad, in Hyderabad, with more than 41 years of experience.

His list covers stroke treatment and recovery, epilepsy and drug-resistant epilepsy, Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease and dementia, multiple sclerosis, motor neuron disease, myasthenia gravis, migraine and chronic headache, diabetic neuropathy, dystonia and tremor disorders. The procedures include EEG, nerve conduction studies and evoked potentials, IV thrombolysis, deep brain stimulation, botulinum toxin therapy, IVIG and migraine nerve block.

He read MBBS and took his MD in general medicine at Government Medical College, Srinagar, between 1975 and 1985, and his DM in neurology at PGIMER Chandigarh from 1985 to 1990. His stroke fellowship was at the National Institutes of Health in Maryland from 1994 to 1996.

Stroke is the thread through the rest of his record. He is a past president of the Indian Stroke Association, a Fellow of the American Stroke Association, and IV thrombolysis appears on his own list, the emergency treatment that a two-year NIH stroke fellowship in the mid-1990s would have covered as it was entering practice.

He has also been president of the Indian Academy of Neurology and of the Andhra Pradesh Neuroscientists Association, and is a Fellow of the Indian Academy of Neurology, of the American Academy of Neurology and of the Royal College of Physicians of Glasgow.

The Government of Telangana gave him its State Teachers Award in 2017, recognition for teaching rather than for clinical work. He has also worked at Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences in Hyderabad.

dr-puppala-sri-sai-srujana.bio:
Dr. Puppala Sri Sai Srujana is a Consultant Neurologist at KIMS Hospitals, Secunderabad, in Hyderabad, with more than 6 years of experience. Her profile records neurology together with neuromuscular disorders.

Her list covers myasthenia gravis, motor neuron disease, multiple sclerosis and diabetic neuropathy on the neuromuscular side, with nerve conduction studies, evoked potentials and IVIG behind them. It also covers epilepsy and drug-resistant epilepsy with EEG, stroke treatment and IV thrombolysis, migraine and chronic headache with nerve block, and Parkinson's disease, dystonia and tremor disorders with deep brain stimulation and botulinum toxin therapy.

She read MBBS at Kamineni Institute of Medical Sciences, took her MD in general medicine at Kasturba Medical College in Mangalore, and the DrNB in neurology at KIMS Secunderabad, where she now practises. Her post-doctoral fellowship in neuromuscular disorders was at the Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology in Trivandrum. She also holds an international certification in epilepsy for neurologists from Thomas Jefferson University, a certification in epilepsy from the Indian Epilepsy Society, and a certification in headache from the Indian Academy of Neurology.

Her awards map onto the same two subjects. She received the Dr. Surat Mohan Das Award for the best paper in autoimmune neurology and a certificate of commendation for her DNB thesis, both for work on neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders, and the Prof. M. Gourie Devi Award for the best paper in neuromuscular disorders, on idiopathic inflammatory myopathies. In 2023 she received the Dr. P.V. Chalapathi Rao Memorial Award as best outgoing superspeciality resident.
